headline: PUMA EXPLORATION SAMPLES 16.38 G/T GOLD SOUTH OF RIM — New Veins Mirror High-Grade System; McKenzie Trend Extends at New Brunswick Project
snippet: Puma Exploration (TSX-V: PUMA) reported a surface sample grading 16.38 g/t gold from a new vein south of its RIM zone at the McKenzie Gold Project in northern New Brunswick, with the company noting the new structures are geologically similar to the high-grade RIM veins — suggesting the gold system extends beyond previously drilled extents. McKenzie is Puma's flagship discovery, which has returned multi-gram intercepts from successive drill programs; identifying new RIM-analogous structures south of the known system expands the district-scale potential and provides targets for the company's next drill campaign. At current gold prices above $3,600/oz, high-grade vein systems in Atlantic Canada are increasingly attracting capital from both retail and institutional sources.

headline: SPC NICKEL CONFIRMS HIGH-GRADE Cu-Ni-PGM COINCIDENT WITH NEW EM CONDUCTORS — 2 New Sulphide Occurrences Discovered at Muskox, Nunavut; 2027 Drill Program Set
snippet: SPC Nickel (TSX-V: SPC) completed its 2026 field season at the Muskox Cu-Ni-PGM project in the Kitikmeot region of Nunavut, confirming high-grade copper-nickel-platinum group metal mineralization coincident with newly identified electromagnetic conductors — and discovering two previously unsampled high-grade sulphide occurrences in the process. The project has returned 2025 surface grab sample grades up to 18.15% Cu, 97.90 g/t Pd and 11.65 g/t Pt, among the highest critical metal concentrations documented at any Canadian exploration project. The 2026 geophysical and sampling work now generates drill-ready targets for a 2027 program, transforming Muskox from a surface anomaly into a systematically de-risked drill candidate with PGM grades that rival producing Sudbury operations.

headline: AUMEGA METALS DISCOVERS PORPHYRY SYSTEM AT CAPE RAY — New Search Space Opens Across NL Property; Earlier Cu Grabs Hit 17%
snippet: AuMEGA Metals (TSX-V: AUM) announced the discovery of a porphyry-style mineralizing system at its Cape Ray property in southwest Newfoundland, opening a new geological search space across the land package — which had previously been explored primarily for high-grade gold shear zone targets. The company's earlier geochemical work at Cape Ray had returned surface copper grab samples up to 17%, consistent with porphyry copper-gold systems. With the first drill holes completed at the Isle aux Morts Granite and Cape Ray West zones in 2026, the identification of an overarching porphyry system now provides a district-scale structural framework that could unify multiple targets — a material re-rating event for investors who were viewing Cape Ray as a single-vein gold story.

headline: ALEX METALS EXPANDS SE ALASKA VMS LAND BY 150% — Strong 2026 Field Season Triggers Major Staking at Underexplored Corridor
snippet: Alex Metals (TSX-V: ALX) staked additional claims to increase its southeast Alaska volcanogenic massive sulphide land package by 150% following a strong 2026 field season, citing new geological evidence supporting district-scale VMS prospectivity in the corridor. Southeast Alaska is home to several large VMS systems including the past-producing Greens Creek mine — North America's largest primary silver mine — giving the land package direct geological analogues for high-grade polymetallic discovery. A 150% expansion after positive field results is a meaningful capital commitment that signals the company's technical team believes it has identified more than one viable drill target.

headline: ARIZONA GOLD & SILVER DOUBLES DRILL CAPACITY AT PHILADELPHIA — Second Rig Arrives as Mohave County Gold-Silver Program Accelerates
snippet: Arizona Gold & Silver (TSX-V: AZS) added a second drill rig at its Philadelphia gold-silver project in Mohave County, Arizona, doubling the company's drilling capacity mid-program and signaling confidence in the project's near-term discovery potential. Philadelphia sits in the prolific Arizona gold corridor where multiple historical producers operated at high grades; the company's 2026 program has been systematically testing strike and depth extensions of known mineralization. Adding a rig mid-season — a capital-intensive decision — typically reflects that early holes are encountering more than expected and the company wants to follow up quickly before year-end.

headline: USA RARE EARTH SURGES 13%, ANTIMONY +9%, MP MATERIALS +6% — Critical Minerals Rebound With Market; Sector Still Below Week-Ago Levels
snippet: USA Rare Earth (NASDAQ: USAR) rallied 13% to $7.09 on November 23 as critical minerals stocks moved higher with the broader market recovery, with United States Antimony gaining 9% and MP Materials adding 6% in the same session. Despite the relief rally, every name in the group still traded below week-ago levels following a broad November selloff driven by tech sector weakness and rising interest rate expectations. The divergence between sector price action and strategic importance — Trump's pledge to match China on rare earths within 10 months remains in force — creates the kind of dislocation that historically precedes re-ratings once sentiment stabilizes.

headline: CERRADO GOLD POSTS $33.8M QUARTERLY EBITDA, ACQUIRES MANANTIAL ESPEJO MINE IN PATAGONIA FOR $20M
snippet: Cerrado Gold (TSX: CERT) reported quarterly adjusted EBITDA of $33.8 million from its Santa Cruz, Brazil operations and separately announced the acquisition of Minera Tritón Argentina, owner of the past-producing Manantial Espejo mine in Santa Cruz Province, Argentina, for US$20 million cash — adding a second Patagonian jurisdiction to its operational footprint. Manantial Espejo was a producing silver-gold mine until 2022 and retains substantial near-mine resource potential; at current silver and gold prices the asset could be restarted at materially different economics than its prior life. The combination of record quarterly earnings and an opportunistic brownfield acquisition in a jurisdiction with established permitting demonstrates the type of capital discipline that mid-tier gold investors prize at this stage of the cycle.

headline: NEM VS. KGC: KINROSS FAVOURED ON VALUATION AND LOWER LEVERAGE — Analyst Comparison Finds KGC More Attractive at Current Gold Prices
snippet: A Yahoo Finance analysis comparing Newmont (NYSE: NEM) and Kinross Gold (NYSE/TSX: KGC) for gold mining exposure concludes that Kinross offers a more attractive entry point at current gold prices, based on more favourable valuation multiples and lower balance sheet leverage. With both names down 15–20% from their 2026 highs despite gold remaining above $3,600/oz, the comparison is specifically useful for investors deciding where to allocate gold producer exposure in the current correction. The analysis illustrates a common challenge in the current environment: determining which selloff is a valuation opportunity versus which reflects deteriorating fundamentals at a specific company.

headline: GSP RESOURCE LAUNCHES DRONE MAG SURVEY AT MER — BC Highland Valley Porphyry Copper Target Gets High-Resolution Targeting After Nov. 17 Discovery
snippet: GSP Resource (TSX-V: GSPR) launched a high-resolution drone magnetic survey at its Mer Property in the Highland Valley district of British Columbia, one week after announcing a new near-surface porphyry copper discovery at the site on November 17. Highland Valley hosts Canada's largest copper mine, operated by Teck Resources — giving any porphyry copper discovery in the district an immediate geological and infrastructure context. The rapid follow-up with airborne magnetics indicates the company is treating Mer as a live discovery rather than a background anomaly, with the survey designed to define the full intrusive footprint before prioritising drill targets.

headline: JUNIOR MINING CONSOLIDATION: WHY CAPITAL IS SELECTIVE, NOT SCARCE — M&A Wave Favours Companies With Defined Resources and Strategic Backers
snippet: Discovery Alert's November 2026 analysis examines the ongoing wave of junior mining M&A and argues that acquisition capital is not scarce — it is selective, targeting companies with defined resources, strong technical teams, and strategic investor sponsorship rather than purely cheap valuations. The piece identifies three common attributes of juniors being acquired at premiums in 2026: tight share structures, management with operational track records, and projects in jurisdictions where acquirers already have operating infrastructure. For self-directed retail investors, the analysis offers a practical checklist for distinguishing acquisition candidates from value traps in the current environment where the GDXJ has drawn down 20% from its highs.
